To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

arts-based methods are a way of working with participants, broadly conceived, to know and intervene in the alcohol and other drug problem in ways that are generative, collaborative, embodied, and sensorial, and that are created specultively together with the audience and the environment.

(i) arts based methods can be used as a research tool to explore the ways in which people who identify as dependent or addicted make and perform their problems in their everyday lives; (ii) arts based research can help people who identify as being dependent or addicted to explore the ways they are affected by the problem of dependency or addiction; and (iii) arts based methods have the potential to help people who identify themselves as dependent or addicted to find ways of dealing with the problem of dependency and/or
the arts and arts based research methods can be used to create and enact new realities and new ways to know and intervene in alcohol and other drug related problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to make the problems we seek to know in ways that do not simply reproduce the same old problems.
what we might learn by "making problems" rather than "solving problems." (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
how we make problems in order to make things better.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the arts and arts-based methods have great potential for alcohol and other drug research to develop in more generative and collaborative (with participants) ways, allowing research to be more intimate with alcohol and other drug problem worlds.

arts based research is not only a method of choice for critical studies of alcohol, but it is also an essential component of the critical drug studies project. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the arts and arts based approaches are an important part of the critical drug studies toolkit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found the arts to be an excellent means of creating and sustaining collaborative, generative relationships with participants, which in turn has led to the production of new and innovative knowledge about the nature of alcohol and other substance related problems and the ways in which they are addressed.
the arts are a method for making problems.
the arts allow us to "make" problems in new ways and thus to "make" new problems in the first place.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the arts can be a generative way of making problems, which can then be made to be known in ways that can help us to know and intervene in the world in new ways.
we can use the arts to make new kinds of knowledge about drug problems that are more collaborative, more embodied, and more generative.

the arts and arts-based methods have the potential to help us know and intervene with alcohol and other drugs and the people who use them in more collaborative and inventive ways, thus allowing us to know and intervene in ways that are more generative and less violent.
